# Every theory through the same exam. Findings 004

*Generated by `uv run python -m knots_sim.exam` (inputs 0421b9d00eac, commit 14f3930).
Every number comes from that run. The exam is `sim/observations/spec.yaml`, sealed v3 on 2026-09-27
(SHA-256 b4b0c5eadf27…); the harness is `sim/knots_sim/exam.py`; each theory's mapping onto the trials is written
out at the top of its file in `sim/knots_sim/theories/`, for its proponents to check. The site shows the same matrix at
/research/#exam.*

## In brief

Three of six theories have sat the exam: T1 Perforators (drive, movement, both, both+adaptation); T3 Trigger points (drive, drive+stretch); T6 Perception (arousal). Each part was scored in 32 settings sampled across the theory's own
plausible ranges; a cell is the share of settings in which the part holds. It says what each theory can do, never which is
true.

- **All at once.** The best joint pass, every scored part in one setting, is 0%. No variant does everything the reports describe.
- **Only one can:** O8.1 form a new knot nearby after a release (Perception, in 5 of 32 settings); O15 have a unit as dense as micro knots (Perforators, in 32 of 32 settings).
- **How many.** Perforators: 18,750 knots in a body where it holds any, of 100,000 units, and none at all in 47% of settings; Trigger points: 171 knots in a body where it holds any, of 300 units, and none at all in 31% of settings; Perception: no unit to count. Practitioners who count report hundreds of thousands.
- **The hand (open, Q1).** Pressed, with a slow out-breath, a knot often lets go within seconds; the author could not say whether under the hand or as it eases off, so the exam takes either (v2). The theories split on it: Perforators lets 0% go under the hand and 98% as it lifts; Trigger points lets 66% go under the hand and 6% as it lifts; Perception lets 0% go under the hand and 46% as it lifts.

## How many knots each would hold

The share of the theory's units holding a knot after 30 minutes of held stress in the patch, times the units a body has by its own sources: as if the whole body were held like the patch, so an upper figure.

| theory | units in a body | knots (median) | where it holds any | 10–90% of settings | settings with none |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Perforators | 100,000 | 1,562 | 18,750 | 0–31,094 | 47% |
| Trigger points | 300 | 155 | 171 | 0–187 | 31% |
| Perception | none: The account has no unit to count: knots are places made tender, as many as the body map resolves. | | | | |

## When a pressed knot lets go (Q1, open)

A press held a minute with slow breaths, then lifted: the share of each model's knots (over its settings and the knot depths) that let go under the hand, within 5 s of the lift, later, or not within 30 s. The reports cannot say which happens; it is the cheapest observation that would tell the theories apart.

| T1 movement | 119 | 0% | 98% | 0% | 2% | – |

| T1 both+adaptation | 119 | 0% | 98% | 0% | 2% | – |

| T3 drive+stretch | 154 | 92% | 2% | 1% | 5% | 17 s |

The exam's first version was scored with the hand still pressing (the harness's reading of O2, stricter than its words), and no theory passed it (findings 004 at commit c4cd6f9); version 2 takes a hand that holds or one that eases off halfway through the out-breath.

## Each theory

### T1 Perforators

Variants: *drive*, the breath acts through sympathetic drive to the skin's small arteries; *movement*, the breath acts through the tissue's movement at the knot; *both*, through drive and movement together; *both+adaptation*, both, with the muscle adapting to a held length over hours (knots can set).

- In at least half the settings (its best variant): O4.1, O15.
- In some settings: O1.1, O1.2, O1.3, O1.4, O1.5, O2.1, O2.2, O4.2, O16.1, O16.2, O6, O13, O10.1.
- In none of 32: O8.1.
- Silent: O3. Not run yet: O5, O8.2, O9, O10.2.
- O3: Nothing in the vessel switch turns on hydration.
- O15: Small vessels rise to the skin one every 4-5 mm, on the order of 100,000 (taylor1987, saintcyr2009).
- O1.3: Through drive alone the breath is not local, so focusing it changes nothing; through movement, focus concentrates the movement at the place.
- O2.2: Pressed, the vessel is squeezed and cannot open: it lets go within a second of the hand lifting, not under it.
- O8.1: A release lowers the pressure its siblings share, by several mmHg, but not enough to shut one; a neighbour shuts only if something else pushes on it by 10 mmHg or more (exploratory/2026-09-27-migration-pressure.py), where tissue pressure under the skin rises only a few mmHg as it fills (christ1997).
- O10.1: Without adaptation nothing remembers how long a knot was held; with it, a knot held for hours can set and hold at rest (findings 003).

### T3 Trigger points

Variants: *drive*, the breath acts as relaxation lowering motor drive (the account's own); *drive+stretch*, and the breath's movement stretches the band.

- In at least half the settings (its best variant): O4.1.
- In some settings: O1.1, O1.2, O1.3, O1.4, O1.5, O2.1, O2.2, O4.2, O16.1, O16.2, O6, O13.
- In none of 32: O8.1, O15.
- Silent: O3. Not run yet: O5, O8.2, O9, O10.1, O10.2.
- O3: Nothing in the energy crisis turns on hydration.
- O10.1: Its slow sustaining factors (weeks) are not modelled yet.
- O15: Hundreds of sites, a few regions in each muscle (300 taken as representative); the active nidus is 1-2 mm (hubbard1993).
- O8.1: New knots after a release come from the taut band's load shifting to its neighbours: an extension of the account.
- O2.2: Pressure release takes tens of seconds (60-90 s at the pressures used, pecosmartin2019), not one out-breath.
- O4.2: Which endplates hold a knot is set more by their own activity than by where stress is held.

### T6 Perception

Variants: *arousal*, the breath eases arousal and is felt as safety; attention and pressure act on what is felt at a place.

- In at least half the settings (its best variant): O4.1, O4.2, O16.1.
- In some settings: O1.2, O1.3, O1.4, O1.5, O2.1, O16.2, O8.1, O13, O10.1.
- In none of 32: O1.1, O2.2, O6.
- Silent: O3, O15. Not run yet: O5, O8.2, O9, O10.2.
- O3: Nothing in the account turns on hydration.
- O15: The account has no unit to count: knots are places made tender, as many as the body map resolves.
- O6: Its tingling comes from overbreathing, in the hands, face and trunk at once (macefield1991), not at a release.
- O1.1: Its easy knots fade on the in-breath, when pain is felt less (arsenault2013), not on the out-breath.
- O2.2: A press adds input and draws attention, so a pressed knot is felt more: it fades, if at all, when the hand lifts, not under it.

## Corrections since the first run (26 Sep 2026)

- *O8 (now O8.1) for the perforators never ran.* Its sibling test put the knot to be released on the thinnest wall, which cannot hold one, so its zeros said nothing. Found on the author's question about migration (27 Sep 2026); the knot is now the thickest-walled sibling, as in the parent test, and every trial with a precondition reports in how many settings it ran (a test fails if one never does).
- *Perception's cluster trials (O8, O13) never ran either.* Its worked knot was pressed until it let go, and a press makes a knot felt more, so it never did. Every theory's knot is now worked for a minute (press, attention, slow breaths) and then the hand lifts; the check that each trial ran caught it.
- *O2.2 read the hand as still pressing*, stricter than the words; the author could not say which, and exam v2 takes either.

Trials that ran, per theory and variant: T1 drive O8.1 in 10 of 32; T1 drive O13 in 12 of 32; T1 movement O8.1 in 11 of 32; T1 movement O13 in 13 of 32; T1 both O8.1 in 11 of 32; T1 both O13 in 14 of 32; T1 both+adaptation O8.1 in 11 of 32; T1 both+adaptation O13 in 14 of 32; T3 drive O8.1 in 22 of 32; T3 drive O13 in 22 of 32; T3 drive+stretch O8.1 in 22 of 32; T3 drive+stretch O13 in 22 of 32; T6 arousal O8.1 in 12 of 32; T6 arousal O13 in 12 of 32.

## How the trials were made fair

Found by running the first three theories; each applies to every theory, the ones not yet built included, and any later change reruns them all (sim/PLAN.md §5b).

- *One rule for the stress unit.* 1 is a surge that forms knots, and the holding stress (0.4–0.7) keeps them. Each theory
  sets its one scale so that the typical place that can hold a knot, where stress is held most, sits in the middle of its
  window: the surge makes it a knot, the holding stress keeps it one and cannot make it one alone.
- *Local trials start after 30 broad breaths*, once the easy knots have gone, so that what a focused breath or a press lets
  go is its own.
- *Easy and hard knots are read from a population:* the patch's own knots under 30 broad breaths (O1.5).
- *Time to form.* The surge lasts 3 minutes and the count is taken after 30 minutes at a stress, since some theories' knots
  form over slow loops.
- *Minutes of slow breathing calm* (oneda2010, adler2019): every theory whose breath acts through drive gets that sustained
  fall as well as each breath's dip; zero is in its range.
- *Each press as its own literature has it:* the trigger point's pressure release is calibrated to its quoted 60–90 s.
- *Sparks within 10 s*, the sealed reading of "within seconds".

## Limits

- A zero is none of 32 settings, not impossible; one setting is 3%. Where a zero is structural, the theory's notes say so.
- The trials read the sealed words one way (the `readings` in the spec); another reading could move a cell, and would be a new,
  dated version of the exam.
- Each theory is one formalisation of its account, in its strongest form as `src/data/hypotheses.ts` states it, with variants
  where the equations are a choice. Its proponents may formalise it otherwise; the mapping is written out to be checked.
- The vascular latch, densification and the nerve view are not modelled yet; mirroring (O9), stiffness (O5) and accumulation
  with age (O10.2) need the mechanics and body stages.
